topic: Binance incident cross-chain freeze timeline and explicit XRPL coverage boundary

primary_source.title: Four Hours, 20 Freezes, One Attacker: Inside the Race to Freeze the Binance Hack, Second by Second
primary_source.method: Direct public blockchain reads, issuer freeze events and balances at freeze blocks; address labels from public explorer tags.
primary_source.critical_scope_limit: The report explicitly did not read XRPL, Bitcoin, Solana, Optimism and other chains. It cannot independently verify the 233.46M XRP tranche or the six XRPL recipient wallets.

timeline_utc.event: Main Binance 14 drain; one transaction moved 167,464 ETH, 1.62B USDT and dozens of other tokens.
About 700M USDT left the main attacker address before Tether's freeze; approximately 205M was later frozen downstream.
Tether blacklisted the main attacker address 37 minutes after the drain.
Circle froze approximately 823M USDC at the main attacker address, 41 minutes after the drain.
Tether froze approximately 312.7M USDT at the main address plus approximately 66.0M one hop downstream.
Tether Gold freeze: 12,574 XAUt, valued by the report at approximately $50.6M.
Ripple paused approximately 40.5M RLUSD across three wallets; the report says approximately 48M had already moved.
PAXG freeze: 1,907 oz, valued at approximately $7.7M.
Binance moved 29,934 WBETH, valued at approximately $76.9M, to a wallet where it was frozen.
Arbitrum Security Council moved 74.6M ARB and 8,426 ETH to a frozen holding wallet.
Circle froze a second attacker-linked wallet holding approximately 123,176 USDC.

tether.note: The later Ethereum amount includes approximately $204M more USDT that reached the blacklisted address and was frozen on arrival. The $378.7M Tron amount is a subset of Tether's cross-chain total, not an additional amount.

circle.note: The report excludes the approximately $60M USDC in Binance's own compromised wallets from its approximately $2.8B attacker-address total. The second wallet and Binance-wallet freezes are separate observations.

ripple.note: The report's RLUSD observation is Ethereum-specific. It explicitly says XRPL RLUSD was not read.

later_reuters_reconciliation.interpretation: Reuters attributes a later >$1.1B USDC freeze statement to Circle. The October 30 onchain report documents $823M at the main attacker address plus the listed separate freezes, which still do not fully reconcile to >$1.1B. Further later freezes or broader scope may explain the difference; exact address/contract reconciliation is unavailable. Preserve both snapshots and do not add them.

unfreezable_asset_context.note: These are Ethereum attacker-funded wallets and are unrelated to the XRP recipient balances. ETH on Ethereum has no issuer freeze control or chain-level emergency council comparable to Arbitrum's.

relationship_and_causal_implications: Circle, Tether and Ripple issuer controls operated as emergency brakes for their own token contracts, not for native XRP.
Tether's 378.7M Tron freeze is included in its 1.5695B cross-chain total and must not be double-counted.
The reported Circle >1.1B USDC figure is later and broader than the October 30 823M main-address observation; scope is unresolved.
The Arbitrum Security Council intervention is a chain-governance action, not a stablecoin issuer freeze.
The report's explicit omission of XRPL means it is not independent corroboration of the 233.46M XRP theft or later six-wallet redistribution.
No freeze amount proves recovery, return to Binance, or market purchase.
next_actions: Obtain the report's full freeze list and verify each token/chain/contract/address against raw public transaction receipts.
Reconcile Circle's later >$1.1B statement to subsequent USDC blacklist events by address and chain.
Reconcile Tether's Tron 378.7M subset to its 1.5695B cross-chain total.
Keep XRPL attacker-recipient monitoring on a separate native-ledger data path; do not use the OnChain Benchmark report as XRPL corroboration.
safety: Public chain data and public reporting only; no unauthorized access, wallet interaction, or asset movement.
